note: Generated by `npm run build:hooks` from the authored files in hooks/. Edit those, not this.

AUS.hook: The only country that is also a continent, and more than 80% of its mammals, reptiles and frogs live nowhere else.
AUS.place: The continent-sized island between the Indian and Pacific oceans, below Indonesia and Papua New Guinea.

NZL.hook: One of the last large landmasses humans reached, settled only around 1300 — and it had no land mammals at all except bats.
NZL.place: Two main islands about 2,000km southeast of Australia, alone in the South Pacific.

ROU.hook: Speaks a Romance language completely surrounded by Slavic and Hungarian ones — a linguistic island left behind by Rome.
ROU.place: North of Bulgaria on the Black Sea, with the Carpathians curving through its middle and the Danube delta on its edge.

BGR.hook: Grows much of the world's rose oil in the Valley of the Roses — it takes roughly 3,000kg of petals to make one kilogram.
BGR.place: South of Romania on the Black Sea, sitting above Greece and Türkiye.

SRB.hook: Became landlocked overnight in 2006 when Montenegro voted to leave — it kept the Danube and lost the sea.
SRB.place: The landlocked centre of the Balkans, touching eight neighbours.

HRV.hook: Over 1,200 islands, and a shape like a crescent — its coast is cut clean in two by a 20km strip belonging to Bosnia.
HRV.place: The crescent along the Adriatic, curving around Bosnia and Herzegovina.

BIH.hook: Has just 20km of coastline, at Neum — barely a beach, but enough to split Croatia's coast into two pieces.
BIH.place: Inside the Croatian crescent, with one narrow sliver reaching the Adriatic.

ALB.hook: Over 170,000 concrete bunkers were poured across the country under Hoxha — roughly one for every eleven Albanians, and most are still there.
ALB.place: Facing Italy's heel across the Adriatic and Ionian, directly below Montenegro.

MKD.hook: Landlocked, and Lake Ohrid on its border is among the oldest lakes on Earth — roughly 1.3 million years, with species found nowhere else.
MKD.place: Landlocked in the middle of the southern Balkans, between Greece, Bulgaria, Serbia, Kosovo and Albania.

MNE.hook: Its name means black mountain, and the Bay of Kotor cuts so deep inland it is often mistaken for Europe's southernmost fjord.
MNE.place: On the Adriatic between Croatia and Albania.

CUB.hook: The largest island in the Caribbean and the longest — end to end it covers about the distance from London to Edinburgh, yet sits only 145km from Florida.
CUB.place: The long island guarding the mouth of the Gulf of Mexico, directly south of Florida.

DOM.hook: Holds the highest peak in the entire Caribbean, Pico Duarte at 3,101m — high enough that it occasionally gets frost.
DOM.place: The eastern two-thirds of Hispaniola, the island between Cuba and Puerto Rico.

HTI.hook: The only nation founded by a successful slave revolt, in 1804 — and the first independent country in Latin America.
HTI.place: The western third of Hispaniola, sharing one island with the Dominican Republic.

JAM.hook: Its Blue Mountains are steep and wet enough that the coffee grown there sells for several times the world price.
JAM.place: South of Cuba and west of Hispaniola, on its own in the middle of the sea.

TTO.hook: Home to Pitch Lake, the largest natural asphalt deposit on Earth — parts of London and New York are paved with it.
TTO.place: Just 11km off Venezuela's northeast tip, the last stop at the bottom of the island arc.

BHS.hook: Around 700 islands, only about 30 of them inhabited — and the seabed beside the shallow banks drops away to 4,000m.
BHS.place: The long scatter northeast of Cuba, beginning just off the Florida coast.

BRB.hook: Sits out in the Atlantic beyond the island arc rather than in it, which is why hurricanes so often pass it by.
BRB.place: Alone to the east of the chain, past Saint Vincent — the most easterly country in the Caribbean.

LCA.hook: The Pitons rise straight out of the sea as twin volcanic spires — the only place in the Caribbean with a drive-in volcano.
LCA.place: Midway down the eastern arc, between Martinique and Saint Vincent.

DMA.hook: The Nature Island, with the world's second-largest boiling lake — and no relation whatsoever to the Dominican Republic, 800km northwest.
DMA.place: In the eastern arc between Guadeloupe and Martinique. The mix-up with the Dominican Republic is the one to watch for.

VCT.hook: One main island plus 32 smaller ones, and a volcano — La Soufrière — that erupted as recently as 2021.
VCT.place: In the eastern arc, directly between Saint Lucia and Grenada.

ATG.hook: Claims a beach for every day of the year — 365 of them, one for each day.
ATG.place: Near the top of the eastern arc, east of Saint Kitts.

GRD.hook: The Isle of Spice, and one of the world's great nutmeg producers — the nut is on the national flag.
GRD.place: The southern end of the eastern arc, just north of Trinidad.

KNA.hook: The smallest sovereign state in the Americas by both area and population — the whole country would fit inside Liverpool.
KNA.place: Near the top of the eastern arc, northwest of Antigua.

COD.hook: The Congo is the deepest river in the world, over 220m in places — and the country holds most of the world's cobalt.
COD.place: The vast heart of Africa astride the equator, with only a 40km squeeze of Atlantic coast.

AGO.hook: Portuguese-speaking, and split in two — the oil-rich Cabinda exclave is cut off from the rest by a strip of DR Congo.
AGO.place: On the Atlantic below DR Congo, with the separate Cabinda enclave sitting to its north.

TCD.hook: Lake Chad has lost about 90% of its surface area since the 1960s — the country is named after a lake that is nearly gone.
TCD.place: Landlocked in north-central Africa, running from deep Sahara down into the Sahel.

CMR.hook: Called Africa in miniature — desert, rainforest, savanna, mountains and coast in one country, with both English and French official.
CMR.place: At the crook of the Gulf of Guinea, where West Africa turns the corner and heads south.

SSD.hook: The newest country in the world, independent in 2011 — and the Sudd wetland at its centre is among the largest on Earth.
SSD.place: Landlocked below Sudan, between Ethiopia and the Central African Republic.

CAF.hook: Sits almost exactly at the geographic centre of the continent, and is among the least visited countries on the planet.
CAF.place: Landlocked in the middle of Africa, below Chad and above DR Congo.

COG.hook: Its capital Brazzaville faces Kinshasa across the river — the closest pair of capital cities anywhere in the world.
COG.place: On the Atlantic west of DR Congo. This is the smaller Congo; the two stare at each other across the water.

GAB.hook: About 88% forest, and in 2002 it turned a tenth of the entire country into national parks in a single stroke.
GAB.place: On the equator on the Atlantic coast, below Cameroon and west of the Republic of the Congo.

GNQ.hook: The only African country with Spanish as an official language — and its capital is not on the mainland but on an island.
GNQ.place: A mainland slice plus islands in the Gulf of Guinea; Malabo sits on Bioko, closer to Cameroon than to its own territory.

STP.hook: Two volcanic islands on the equator that were once the largest cocoa producer in the world — from almost nothing to first place and back.
STP.place: In the Gulf of Guinea off Gabon, straddling the equator.

GTM.hook: The world's largest exporter of cardamom, a spice barely used in its own kitchens — almost the entire crop is shipped to the Middle East.
GTM.place: The first link in the Central American chain, directly south of Mexico.

HND.hook: The original banana republic — the phrase was coined for it in 1904, when US fruit companies effectively ran the country.
HND.place: The wide part of the isthmus, between Guatemala and Nicaragua, with a long Caribbean coast.

NIC.hook: Largest country in Central America, and its lake has bull sharks — they swim up the San Juan river from the Caribbean and stay.
NIC.place: The middle of the isthmus, between Honduras and Costa Rica.

PAN.hook: The isthmus runs east-west, not north-south — so in Panama City the sun rises over the Pacific and sets over the Atlantic.
PAN.place: The S-bend at the bottom of Central America, joining the continent to Colombia.

CRI.hook: Abolished its army in 1948 and put the money into schools and hospitals — it has not had one since.
CRI.place: Between Nicaragua and Panama, near the bottom of the isthmus.

SLV.hook: The smallest country in mainland Americas, and the only one in Central America with no Caribbean coast at all.
SLV.place: Pacific side only, wedged between Guatemala and Honduras.

BLZ.hook: The only Central American country with English as its official language, and home to the largest barrier reef in the northern hemisphere.
BLZ.place: The small notch on the Caribbean side, east of Guatemala and just below Mexico's Yucatán.

KAZ.hook: The largest landlocked country in the world — bigger than all of Western Europe, and Russia's border with it is the longest continuous land border anywhere.
KAZ.place: The vast steppe below Russia, stretching from the Caspian east to China.

UZB.hook: One of only two doubly landlocked countries on Earth — every route to the sea crosses at least two borders. The other is Liechtenstein.
UZB.place: The centre of Central Asia, touching all four of its neighbours and Afghanistan.

TKM.hook: The Darvaza gas crater has been burning since 1971, when geologists set it alight expecting it to go out in weeks.
TKM.place: On the Caspian's eastern shore, mostly the Karakum desert, below Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

TJK.hook: Over 90% mountain — the Pamirs are so high and remote the road through them is nicknamed the roof of the world.
TJK.place: The southeastern corner of Central Asia, squeezed between Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, China and Afghanistan.

KGZ.hook: Lake Issyk-Kul is the second-largest mountain lake in the world and never freezes, despite sitting at 1,600m in the Tian Shan.
KGZ.place: The mountainous strip along China's western border, above Tajikistan.

CHN.hook: Borders fourteen countries, tied with Russia for the most on Earth — yet the whole country runs on a single time zone.
CHN.place: The eastern bulk of Asia, from the Pacific coast west to the Himalaya and the Central Asian deserts.

MNG.hook: The least densely populated sovereign country on Earth — about two people per square kilometre, and more horses than people.
MNG.place: Landlocked between Russia and China, with nothing else touching it.

ETH.hook: Never colonised, and it keeps its own calendar — thirteen months, and about seven years behind the one the rest of the world uses.
ETH.place: The highlands of the Horn of Africa, landlocked since Eritrea broke away in 1993.

TZA.hook: Kilimanjaro rises 5,895m straight off the plain with no range around it — the tallest freestanding mountain on Earth.
TZA.place: On the Indian Ocean below Kenya, with Zanzibar offshore and Lake Victoria at its northwestern corner.

KEN.hook: The Great Rift Valley runs straight through it — the same crack in the continent that will eventually split Africa in two.
KEN.place: On the Indian Ocean astride the equator, between Somalia and Tanzania.

MOZ.hook: One of very few country names containing all five vowels — and its coast faces Madagascar across a 400km channel.
MOZ.place: The long Indian Ocean coast below Tanzania, curving around toward South Africa.

MDG.hook: Broke away from Africa about 160 million years ago, and roughly 90% of its wildlife lives nowhere else on Earth.
MDG.place: The huge island off Mozambique — the fourth largest in the world.

UGA.hook: The White Nile begins here, flowing out of Lake Victoria and then running 6,000km north to the Mediterranean.
UGA.place: Landlocked on the equator between Kenya and DR Congo, on Lake Victoria's northern shore.

ZMB.hook: Shares Victoria Falls with Zimbabwe — the largest single sheet of falling water in the world, and its spray is visible from 50km away.
ZMB.place: Landlocked in south-central Africa above Zimbabwe, touching eight neighbours.

SOM.hook: Has the longest coastline of any country in mainland Africa — over 3,000km wrapping around the Horn.
SOM.place: The Horn itself, curving around Ethiopia from the Gulf of Aden to the Indian Ocean.

ZWE.hook: Named after Great Zimbabwe, a stone city built entirely without mortar — the largest ancient structure south of the Sahara.
ZWE.place: Landlocked between Zambia and South Africa, sharing Victoria Falls along its northern border.

MWI.hook: Lake Malawi holds more fish species than any other lake on Earth — several hundred of them found nowhere else.
MWI.place: A long thin landlocked country wrapped around its own lake, between Zambia, Tanzania and Mozambique.

ERI.hook: Asmara is a near-intact Italian modernist city, built in the 1930s and now a World Heritage site.
ERI.place: On the Red Sea directly above Ethiopia — this is the coastline Ethiopia lost in 1993.

RWA.hook: The land of a thousand hills — and it banned plastic bags back in 2008, long before anyone else did.
RWA.place: Small and landlocked, between DR Congo, Uganda, Tanzania and Burundi.

BDI.hook: One of the most densely populated countries in Africa, and the southernmost headwater of the Nile rises inside it.
BDI.place: Landlocked directly below Rwanda, on the northeastern shore of Lake Tanganyika.

DJI.hook: Lake Assal is the lowest point in Africa and one of the saltiest bodies of water anywhere — saltier than the Dead Sea.
DJI.place: A small country on the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, wedged between Eritrea, Ethiopia and Somalia.

MUS.hook: The dodo lived here and only here, and was gone within about eighty years of humans first landing.
MUS.place: An island in the Indian Ocean roughly 900km east of Madagascar.

COM.hook: Supplies most of the world's ylang-ylang — the flower essence at the heart of Chanel No. 5.
COM.place: A small archipelago in the channel between Mozambique and Madagascar.

SYC.hook: The smallest population of any African country, and its coco de mer palm grows the largest seed in the plant kingdom.
SYC.place: 115 islands in the Indian Ocean, northeast of Madagascar.

UKR.hook: The largest country lying entirely within Europe, sitting on roughly a third of the world's black-earth chernozem soil.
UKR.place: North of the Black Sea, filling the space between Poland and Russia.

BLR.hook: About 40% forest, and it shares the Białowieża primeval woodland — and its bison — with Poland.
BLR.place: Landlocked between Poland and Russia, directly above Ukraine.

MDA.hook: One of the most wine-dependent economies anywhere — the Cricova cellars alone run for over 120km underground, with streets and traffic signs.
MDA.place: The small landlocked country wedged between Romania and Ukraine.

JPN.hook: Nearly 14,000 islands, and three quarters of the land is mountain — almost everyone is packed onto the coastal fringe.
JPN.place: The arc of islands off the Asian mainland, east of the Korean peninsula.

KOR.hook: Went from one of the world's poorest countries to one of its richest inside a single lifetime — the fastest such climb on record.
KOR.place: The southern half of the Korean peninsula, facing Japan across a narrow strait.

PRK.hook: The 4km-wide strip separating it from the South has been left alone so long it has become an accidental wildlife refuge.
PRK.place: The northern half of the Korean peninsula, bordering China along the Yalu river.

TUR.hook: Straddles two continents, which makes Istanbul the only major city in the world with a European half and an Asian half.
TUR.place: The land bridge between Europe and Asia, Black Sea above, Mediterranean below.

SAU.hook: The largest country on Earth with no rivers — not one permanent watercourse anywhere in it.
SAU.place: Most of the Arabian peninsula, Red Sea to the west, the Gulf to the east.

IRQ.hook: Mesopotamia, the land between the Tigris and Euphrates — writing, the wheel and the city were all invented here.
IRQ.place: Between Iran and Syria, with a narrow squeeze of coast at the head of the Gulf.

YEM.hook: Its island of Socotra has been isolated so long that a third of its plants grow nowhere else — including trees that bleed red sap.
YEM.place: The southwestern corner of Arabia, on the strait where the Red Sea meets the Gulf of Aden.

SYR.hook: Damascus has been continuously inhabited for perhaps 11,000 years, which makes it a contender for the oldest city on Earth.
SYR.place: On the eastern Mediterranean between Türkiye and Jordan, with Iraq to the east.

OMN.hook: Its detached northern tip controls the Strait of Hormuz, the 33km gap that about a fifth of the world's oil must pass through.
OMN.place: The southeastern corner of Arabia, with the Musandam exclave cut off by the UAE.

JOR.hook: Its Dead Sea shore is the lowest dry land on the planet, about 430m below sea level — and dropping about a metre a year.
JOR.place: Between the West Bank and Iraq, with one small outlet to the Red Sea at Aqaba.

AZE.hook: The name means Land of Fire, and the gas seeps at Yanar Dag have been burning on the hillside for centuries.
AZE.place: On the Caspian's western shore below Russia, with the Nakhchivan exclave cut off by Armenia.

ARE.hook: A federation of seven emirates, and home to the Burj Khalifa — still the tallest building in the world by a wide margin.
ARE.place: On the southern shore of the Gulf, between Saudi Arabia and Oman.

GEO.hook: Has been making wine for about 8,000 years, fermenting it in clay vessels buried in the ground — the oldest such tradition known.
GEO.place: Between the Black Sea and the Caucasus, below Russia and above Armenia and Türkiye.

ISR.hook: Recycles around 90% of its wastewater, far more than any other country — the next best manages barely a quarter.
ISR.place: A narrow strip on the eastern Mediterranean, between Lebanon and Egypt's Sinai.

LBN.hook: The cedar on its flag once supplied timber to Egypt and Phoenicia for millennia — only a few ancient groves are left standing.
LBN.place: A narrow coastal strip on the eastern Mediterranean, squeezed between Syria and Israel.

ARM.hook: The first state anywhere to adopt Christianity, in 301 — and its national symbol, Mount Ararat, sits across a closed border in Türkiye.
ARM.place: Landlocked in the southern Caucasus, ringed by Türkiye, Georgia, Azerbaijan and Iran.

KWT.hook: Its dinar is the highest-valued currency in the world — one buys more than three US dollars.
KWT.place: At the very top of the Gulf, wedged between Iraq and Saudi Arabia.

PSE.hook: Two separated territories with Israel in between — the West Bank and Gaza are about 45km apart with no direct link.
PSE.place: The West Bank inland along the Jordan, and Gaza on the Mediterranean coast beside Egypt.

QAT.hook: Sits on the largest single natural gas field on Earth, which it shares with Iran across the middle of the Gulf.
QAT.place: A thumb of land pointing north into the Gulf from Saudi Arabia.

BHR.hook: First Gulf state to strike oil, and the first to largely run out — it has been diversifying longer than its neighbours have had to.
BHR.place: A small archipelago in the Gulf off Saudi Arabia's east coast, linked by a 25km causeway.

USA.hook: The only country with land borders on just two nations yet coastline on three oceans — the Arctic one courtesy of Alaska, bought from Russia for two cents an acre.
USA.place: The wide middle of North America, Canada above and Mexico below, with Alaska detached in the far northwest corner.

CAN.hook: Has the longest coastline of any country on Earth — about 202,000km, roughly a sixth of the world's total, thanks to a shattered Arctic archipelago.
CAN.place: Everything above the United States, ocean to ocean to ocean. The border it shares with the US is the longest between any two countries.

MEX.hook: Mexico City is sinking as much as 50cm a year in places — it was built on a drained lake bed, and the ground is still compacting under it.
MEX.place: The funnel narrowing southeast from the US border down to the Central American chain.

EGY.hook: About 95% of Egyptians live on roughly 5% of the land — from orbit the inhabited country is a thin green ribbon along the Nile.
EGY.place: The northeast corner of Africa, with the Sinai peninsula reaching across into Asia.

DZA.hook: The largest country in Africa, and about four-fifths of it is Sahara — the population clings to the northern coast.
DZA.place: The middle of the Maghreb coast between Morocco and Tunisia, running deep south into the desert.

SDN.hook: Has more pyramids than Egypt — around 200 of them at Meroë, steeper and narrower, and far less visited.
SDN.place: Below Egypt on the Red Sea, above South Sudan, where the Blue and White Niles meet at Khartoum.

MAR.hook: You can stand on its coast and see Spain — the Strait of Gibraltar is only about 13km across at its narrowest.
MAR.place: The northwest corner of Africa, with both Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts and the Atlas range inland.

LBY.hook: The Great Man-Made River pumps fossil water from under the Sahara through 2,800km of pipe — the largest irrigation project ever built.
LBY.place: On the Mediterranean between Tunisia and Egypt, almost entirely desert behind a thin coastal strip.

TUN.hook: Contains the northernmost point in Africa, and Carthage — Rome's great rival — stood just outside the modern capital.
TUN.place: The small wedge on the Mediterranean between Algeria and Libya, reaching closest to Sicily.

GBR.hook: Nowhere in Britain is more than about 125km from the sea — no point on the island is genuinely inland.
GBR.place: The large island off northwest France, plus Northern Ireland across the Irish Sea.

SWE.hook: Has roughly 270,000 islands, more than any other country, though barely a thousand of them are lived on.
SWE.place: The eastern half of the Scandinavian peninsula, Norway to the west, Baltic Sea to the east.

FIN.hook: Counts about 188,000 lakes, and its language is related to neither Swedish nor Russian — it is not Indo-European at all.
FIN.place: East of Sweden, sharing a 1,340km border with Russia — the longest in the EU.

NOR.hook: The fjords fold its coastline out to about 100,000km — more than twice the distance around the Earth.
NOR.place: The western spine of Scandinavia, running up the Atlantic side from Denmark to the Arctic.

IRL.hook: Has no native snakes, and far more people of Irish descent live abroad than on the island itself.
IRL.place: The western island of the British Isles, across the Irish Sea from Britain.

DNK.hook: Over 400 islands and a peninsula, and no point in the country is further than about 52km from the sea.
DNK.place: The peninsula and islands above Germany, corking the entrance to the Baltic. Greenland and the Faroes are its territories.

LTU.hook: Was once the largest country in Europe — the medieval Grand Duchy stretched from the Baltic all the way to the Black Sea.
LTU.place: The southernmost of the three Baltic states, sitting directly above Poland.

LVA.hook: Riga holds the largest concentration of Art Nouveau architecture anywhere in the world.
LVA.place: The middle of the three Baltic states, between Estonia and Lithuania.

EST.hook: The first country in the world to hold a general election online, and more forested now than a century ago.
EST.place: The northernmost Baltic state, across a narrow gulf from Finland.

ISL.hook: Straddles the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and is pulling apart about 2cm a year — and heats nearly every home with geothermal water.
ISL.place: Alone in the North Atlantic between Norway and Greenland, just below the Arctic Circle.

PNG.hook: Over 800 living languages are spoken here — roughly one in eight of all the languages on Earth, in one country.
PNG.place: The eastern half of New Guinea, sharing the island with Indonesia, directly north of Australia.

SLB.hook: Nearly a thousand islands, and Guadalcanal among them — the campaign fought there turned the Pacific war.
SLB.place: A double chain running southeast from Papua New Guinea, northeast of Australia.

FJI.hook: The 180th meridian runs right through it, so the international date line had to be bent around the country to keep it on one day.
FJI.place: About 330 islands in the South Pacific east of Vanuatu — the hub of the region.

VUT.hook: Regularly ranked the most disaster-exposed country on Earth — cyclones, earthquakes and active volcanoes, all at once.
VUT.place: A Y-shaped chain west of Fiji, out in the Coral Sea east of Australia.

WSM.hook: Skipped 30 December 2011 entirely, jumping across the date line so it could share a working week with Australia and New Zealand.

KIR.hook: The only country in all four hemispheres — its islands are scattered over 3.5 million km² of ocean, an area the size of India.
KIR.place: Strung across the central Pacific, straddling both the equator and the date line.

FSM.hook: Nan Madol is a ruined city built on around a hundred artificial islets of stacked basalt — a Venice made of volcanic rock.
FSM.place: A long scatter of islands north of Papua New Guinea, running east from Palau.

TON.hook: The only Pacific nation never colonised, and the only one to keep its own monarchy unbroken through the whole colonial era.
TON.place: In Polynesia south of Samoa and east of Fiji.

MHL.hook: Bikini Atoll absorbed 23 nuclear tests, one of them a thousand times the Hiroshima bomb — the crater is still in the reef.
MHL.place: Two parallel chains of atolls in the central Pacific, north of Kiribati.

PLW.hook: Created the world's first shark sanctuary, and requires every visitor to sign a pledge to the country's children on arrival.
PLW.place: The westernmost Pacific islands, east of the Philippines and north of Indonesia.

TUV.hook: Earns a large slice of national income leasing its .tv internet domain — an accident of the alphabet worth millions a year.
TUV.place: Nine low atolls in the central Pacific north of Fiji, and among the smallest countries anywhere.

NRU.hook: About 21km² and strip-mined for phosphate until most of the interior was left as bare limestone pinnacles — briefly the richest country per head on Earth.
NRU.place: A single island just south of the equator, west of Kiribati.

RUS.hook: Spans eleven time zones — when Monday morning starts in Kaliningrad it is already Monday evening in Kamchatka.
RUS.place: From the Baltic to the Pacific across the whole top of Asia. Kaliningrad is a detached piece between Poland and Lithuania.

NER.hook: Has the youngest population on Earth — around half of Niger is under fifteen.
NER.place: Landlocked and mostly Sahara, sitting directly on top of Nigeria. The two names are the mix-up to watch.

MLI.hook: Timbuktu was a university town when Oxford was new, and its medieval ruler Mansa Musa may have been the richest person who ever lived.
MLI.place: Landlocked across the western Sahel, with the Niger river arcing through its middle.

MRT.hook: Runs one of the longest trains in the world — up to 2.5km of iron ore across the desert, with passengers riding on top of the load.
MRT.place: Where the Sahara meets the Atlantic, above Senegal and west of Mali.

BRA.hook: Borders every country in South America except Chile and Ecuador — ten neighbours, more than any country outside Russia and China.
BRA.place: Fills the whole eastern bulge. If you can draw Brazil, the rest of the continent is the leftovers around it.

ARG.hook: Home to Aconcagua, at 6,961m the highest peak anywhere outside Asia — and it sits barely 100km from the Chilean border.
ARG.place: The long southern wedge below Brazil, sharing the Andes spine with Chile the whole way down.

COL.hook: The only country in South America with coastline on both the Pacific and the Caribbean.
COL.place: The top-left corner of the continent, and the only one that touches Panama — the land bridge to North America.

PER.hook: The Amazon starts here, in Andean meltwater, and runs the width of the continent before reaching the Atlantic in Brazil.
PER.place: Pacific coast, just south of the equator. Ecuador and Colombia above, Chile below, Brazil behind the mountains.

VEN.hook: Angel Falls drops 979m, so tall the water atomises into mist before it lands.
VEN.place: The Caribbean shoulder, east of Colombia. Trinidad sits just off its northeast tip.

CHL.hook: 4,300km long and averages 180km wide — the same proportions as a country stretched from Norway to the Sahara.
CHL.place: The ribbon down the Pacific edge, pinned between the Andes and the ocean for its entire length.

BOL.hook: Landlocked since 1884, and still keeps a navy — it patrols Lake Titicaca and waits for the sea to come back.
BOL.place: The landlocked heart of the continent, ringed by Brazil, Peru, Chile, Argentina and Paraguay.

ECU.hook: Named after the equator, which crosses just north of Quito — the only country named for a line of latitude.
ECU.place: A small Pacific notch between Colombia and Peru. The Galápagos belong to it, 900km out to sea.

PRY.hook: Runs almost entirely on the Itaipú dam and sells the surplus to Brazil, making it one of the world's largest electricity exporters per head.
PRY.place: The other landlocked one, tucked between Bolivia, Brazil and Argentina.

URY.hook: Smaller than every other Spanish-speaking country in South America, with more cattle than people — about four to one.
URY.place: The small wedge on the Atlantic between Brazil and Argentina, across the river from Buenos Aires.

GUY.hook: The only country in South America where English is the official language — and since a 2015 offshore oil strike, among the fastest-growing economies on Earth.
GUY.place: One of the three small countries stacked along the northeast coast, east of Venezuela.

SUR.hook: Dutch-speaking, and the smallest sovereign country in South America — most of it is rainforest almost nobody lives in.
SUR.place: The middle of the three northeastern neighbours: Guyana to its west, French Guiana to its east.

IDN.hook: Over 17,000 islands spread across 5,000km — wider than the United States — and it is moving its capital off Java because Jakarta is sinking.
IDN.place: The great archipelago strung along the equator between mainland Asia and Australia.

PHL.hook: 7,641 islands on the Ring of Fire, and about 20 typhoons a year — more than anywhere else on Earth.
PHL.place: The archipelago north of Indonesia and east of Vietnam, facing the open Pacific.

THA.hook: The only country in Southeast Asia never colonised by a European power — it played the British and French off against each other.
THA.place: The middle of the mainland, between Myanmar and Laos, tailing south down the peninsula toward Malaysia.

VNM.hook: About 1,650km long but as little as 50km wide at its waist — you can drive coast to border in under an hour in the middle.
VNM.place: The eastern edge of the mainland, an S-curve down the coast from China to the Mekong delta.

MMR.hook: Produces the large majority of the world's rubies, from the Mogok valley — and answers to Burma just as often.
MMR.place: The western end of mainland Southeast Asia, between India and Thailand.

MYS.hook: Split clean in two by the South China Sea — half a peninsula, half a slice of Borneo, 640km apart.
MYS.place: Below Thailand on the mainland peninsula, and along the north coast of Borneo beside Indonesia and Brunei.

KHM.hook: Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument on Earth, and Cambodia's is the only national flag anywhere that shows a building.
KHM.place: Between Thailand and Vietnam, opening onto the Gulf of Thailand.

LAO.hook: The only landlocked country in Southeast Asia, and the most heavily bombed country per person in history — unexploded ordnance is still being cleared.
LAO.place: Landlocked between Thailand and Vietnam, the Mekong running down much of its western edge.

TLS.hook: One of the youngest countries on Earth, independent only in 2002 after 24 years of occupation.
TLS.place: The eastern half of Timor at the far end of the Indonesian arc, just north of Australia.

SGP.hook: One of the last true city-states, and about a quarter larger than at independence — the extra land was reclaimed from the sea.
SGP.place: At the tip of the Malay peninsula, on the Strait of Malacca, one of the busiest shipping lanes on Earth.

BRN.hook: Oil wealth means no income tax at all — and the country is split into two separate pieces by Malaysian territory.
BRN.place: Two enclaves on the north coast of Borneo, both entirely surrounded by Malaysia.

ZAF.hook: Has three capital cities at once — Pretoria governs, Cape Town legislates, Bloemfontein judges — and twelve official languages.
ZAF.place: The bottom of the continent, completely surrounding Lesotho and wrapping around Eswatini.

NAM.hook: The Namib is the oldest desert on Earth at around 55 million years, and its Skeleton Coast is littered with shipwrecks.
NAM.place: On the Atlantic between Angola and South Africa, with the Caprivi Strip reaching east toward the Zambezi.

BWA.hook: The Okavango spills into the Kalahari and simply evaporates — one of the few great river deltas that never reaches the sea.
BWA.place: Landlocked above South Africa, between Namibia and Zimbabwe.

LSO.hook: One of only three countries entirely surrounded by a single other country — and its lowest point, at 1,400m, is the highest low point on Earth.
LSO.place: Entirely inside South Africa, up in the Drakensberg mountains.

SWZ.hook: Renamed itself from Swaziland in 2018, partly because it kept being confused with Switzerland — and it remains one of the world's last absolute monarchies.
SWZ.place: A small landlocked kingdom between South Africa and Mozambique.

IND.hook: Runs on a single time zone offset by half an hour from the rest of the world — and is now the most populous country on Earth.
IND.place: The triangle jutting into the Indian Ocean, Himalaya across the top, Pakistan west and Bangladesh east.

PAK.hook: Holds K2 and four more of the world's fourteen 8,000m peaks — a greater concentration than anywhere outside Nepal.
PAK.place: West of India, running from the Arabian Sea up to the Karakoram, with Afghanistan and Iran to the west.

IRN.hook: Persian, not Arabic, and Indo-European rather than Semitic — the language is a closer relative of English than of the languages around it.
IRN.place: Between the Caspian and the Gulf, with Iraq and Türkiye west, Afghanistan and Pakistan east.

BGD.hook: Most of the country is one enormous river delta, barely above sea level — the Ganges and Brahmaputra meet and empty out through it.
BGD.place: Almost entirely surrounded by India, opening south onto the Bay of Bengal.

AFG.hook: The Wakhan Corridor is a finger of land drawn purely to keep the Russian and British empires from touching — it still reaches out to China.
AFG.place: Landlocked between Iran, Pakistan and the Central Asian states, with the Hindu Kush through its middle.

NPL.hook: Holds eight of the world's ten highest mountains, and is the only country whose flag is not a rectangle.
NPL.place: A long strip along the Himalaya, entirely between India and China.

LKA.hook: Produces some of the world's best tea from land that was all coffee until a fungus wiped the crop out in the 1870s.
LKA.place: The island off India's southeastern tip, separated by a strait shallow enough to nearly walk.

BTN.hook: Measures Gross National Happiness alongside GDP, and is one of the few carbon-negative countries — its forests absorb more than it emits.
BTN.place: A small Himalayan kingdom between India and China, east of Nepal.

MDV.hook: The lowest country on Earth — its highest natural point is about 2.4m, lower than most ceilings.
MDV.place: A chain of atolls in the Indian Ocean, southwest of Sri Lanka.

ESP.hook: After Switzerland, the most mountainous country in Europe — Madrid sits at 650m, the highest capital on the continent.
ESP.place: Most of the Iberian peninsula, Portugal down its western side, the Pyrenees sealing it off from France.

ITA.hook: The only country with two entire sovereign states inside it — San Marino in the northeast, Vatican City in the middle of Rome.
ITA.place: The boot kicking into the Mediterranean, Sicily at the toe and Sardinia out to the west.

GRC.hook: Around 6,000 islands, only about 230 of them inhabited, and nowhere on the mainland is more than 137km from the sea.
GRC.place: The southern tip of the Balkans, its islands scattered east across the Aegean toward Türkiye.

PRT.hook: Has the oldest fixed borders in Europe, essentially unchanged since 1297 — and supplies about half the world's cork.
PRT.place: The western strip of Iberia: Atlantic on two sides, Spain on the other two.

CYP.hook: Divided since 1974, which makes Nicosia the last divided capital city in Europe — a buffer zone runs straight through it.
CYP.place: In the eastern Mediterranean south of Türkiye — geographically Asian, politically European.

MLT.hook: The most densely populated country in the EU, on islands with no rivers and no lakes at all.
MLT.place: In the middle of the Mediterranean, about 80km south of Sicily.

AND.hook: No airport, no railway, and two heads of state at once — the President of France and a Spanish bishop share the job.
AND.place: High in the Pyrenees, entirely enclosed by Spain and France.

SMR.hook: Claims to be the oldest surviving republic in the world, founded in 301 — and it is completely surrounded by Italy.
SMR.place: A landlocked enclave inside northeastern Italy, up a mountain near Rimini.

VAT.hook: The smallest country on Earth at 0.49km² — the whole state fits inside a single city, with room for a garden.
VAT.place: Entirely within Rome, on the west bank of the Tiber.

NGA.hook: The most populous country in Africa — about one in six Africans is Nigerian — and Nollywood releases more films a year than Hollywood.
NGA.place: On the Gulf of Guinea at the inner corner of the West African bulge.

CIV.hook: Grows roughly 40% of the world's cocoa — more than the next two countries combined. Also answers to Côte d'Ivoire.
CIV.place: On the Gulf of Guinea between Ghana and Liberia.

GHA.hook: The first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence, in 1957 — and Lake Volta is the largest reservoir on Earth by surface area.
GHA.place: On the Gulf of Guinea, between Ivory Coast and Togo.

BFA.hook: Its name was invented in 1984 and means land of upright people — stitched together from two different local languages.
BFA.place: Landlocked directly above Ghana and Ivory Coast, below Mali and Niger.

SEN.hook: Reaches the westernmost point of mainland Africa, and almost completely surrounds another country — The Gambia.
SEN.place: The Atlantic tip of the West African bulge, wrapped around The Gambia on three sides.

GIN.hook: Holds the world's largest bauxite reserves — and the Niger, Senegal and Gambia rivers all rise in its highlands.
GIN.place: On the Atlantic below Senegal, between Guinea-Bissau and Sierra Leone.

BEN.hook: The birthplace of Vodun, which is an official religion here — and home of the Dahomey kingdom's all-female regiment.
BEN.place: A narrow strip running north from the Gulf of Guinea, between Togo and Nigeria.

SLE.hook: Freetown sits on one of the largest natural harbours in the world, which is why freed slaves were resettled there in 1792.
SLE.place: On the Atlantic coast between Guinea and Liberia.

LBR.hook: Founded by freed American slaves in 1847, making it Africa's oldest republic — and more of the world's shipping flies its flag than almost any other.
LBR.place: On the Atlantic below Sierra Leone, west of Ivory Coast.

TGO.hook: One of Africa's narrowest countries — about 110km wide but 550km long, a strip you can drive across in two hours.
TGO.place: A thin ribbon between Ghana and Benin, running north from the Gulf of Guinea.

GNB.hook: The Bijagós archipelago off its coast is 88 islands, only about twenty of them inhabited — and a biosphere reserve.
GNB.place: A small Atlantic country tucked between Senegal and Guinea.

GMB.hook: The smallest country in mainland Africa — a ribbon of land either side of one river, nowhere more than 50km wide.
GMB.place: Following the Gambia river inland, enclosed by Senegal on every side but the Atlantic.

CPV.hook: Ten volcanic islands that were completely uninhabited until Portuguese ships arrived in 1456 — everyone there descends from later arrivals.
CPV.place: An Atlantic archipelago about 570km west of Senegal, out on its own.

FRA.hook: Spans twelve time zones — more than any other country — because its overseas departments reach from the Pacific to the Caribbean to the Indian Ocean.
FRA.place: The hexagon between the Atlantic and the Alps, Spain beyond the Pyrenees, Germany across the Rhine.

DEU.hook: Borders nine countries, more than any other in Europe — it touches nearly everyone from Denmark round to the Netherlands.
DEU.place: The middle of Europe, running from the North Sea coast down to the Alps.

POL.hook: Holds Białowieża, the last great primeval lowland forest in Europe, and the wild bison that live in it.
POL.place: On the flat plain between Germany and the Baltics — the same corridor that runs unbroken from France to Russia.

HUN.hook: Its language is related to nothing around it — the nearest relatives of Hungarian are Finnish and Estonian, 1,500km north.
HUN.place: The landlocked floor of the Carpathian basin, ringed by seven neighbours.

CZE.hook: Drinks more beer per person than any other country, and has done for three decades running.
CZE.place: Landlocked west of Slovakia, wrapped on three sides by Germany, Poland and Austria.

NLD.hook: About a quarter of it lies below sea level, and much of that is land the Dutch built themselves by pumping the sea out.
NLD.place: The North Sea corner above Belgium and west of Germany.

AUT.hook: Nearly two-thirds Alps, and Vienna is the only capital city with commercial vineyards inside its own boundaries.
AUT.place: Landlocked, the Alpine strip east of Switzerland and south of Germany.

BEL.hook: Antwerp handles the large majority of the world's rough diamonds, in a district a few streets across.
BEL.place: The small country on the North Sea between France and the Netherlands.

CHE.hook: Landlocked and mountainous, yet its rivers drain to three different seas — the North Sea, the Mediterranean and the Black Sea.
CHE.place: The Alpine knot where France, Germany, Austria and Italy all meet.

SVK.hook: Builds more cars per person than any country on Earth — roughly one for every five Slovaks each year.
SVK.place: Landlocked, directly east of Czechia. This is the one with Bratislava; Slovenia is 400km southwest.

SVN.hook: More than half forest, one of the greenest countries in Europe — and it has only about 47km of coast to its name.
SVN.place: At the head of the Adriatic below Austria. Not Slovakia, which is 400km northeast — the classic mix-up.

LUX.hook: The richest country per head on Earth, and nearly half its workforce drives in from France, Belgium and Germany every morning.
LUX.place: Tucked into the corner where Belgium, France and Germany meet.

LIE.hook: Doubly landlocked — you must cross two borders to reach any sea — and it is the world's largest producer of false teeth.
LIE.place: A 25km sliver in the upper Rhine valley, entirely between Switzerland and Austria.

MCO.hook: The most densely populated country on Earth, and small enough to walk end to end in under an hour.
MCO.place: A 2km² notch on the French Riviera coast, close to the Italian border.
